properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued October 28 at 9:18PM EDT by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
At 918 PM EDT/818 PM CDT/, Doppler radar was tracking strong
thunderstorms along a line extending from 7 miles northeast of
Wakefield to near Turtle Flambeau Flowage. Movement was east at 50
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Strong thunderstorms will be near...
Northern Lake Gogebic around 925 PM EDT.
Marenisco around 830 PM CDT.
Bergland around 930 PM EDT.

Other locations impacted by these storms include Thousand Island
Lake, Bond Falls, Presque Isle Reservoir, Pomeroy Lake, and Lake
Gogebic State Park.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 28 at 8:12PM CDT until October 28 at 11:15PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Culberson County in southwestern Texas...

* Until 1115 PM CDT /1015 PM MDT/.

* At 812 PM CDT /712 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...

potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.description:
SVREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
West central Hudspeth County in western Texas...

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued October 28 at 8:08PM CDT by NWS Green Bay WI
properties.description:
At 808 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from 20 miles north of Winchester to 25 miles
northwest of Willow Lake, or extending from 51 miles northwest of
Eagle River to 52 miles west of Rhinelander, moving east at 50 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

The strong thunderstorm will be near...
Winchester around 825 PM CDT.
Rice Creek Natural Area around 835 PM CDT.
Lac Du Flambeau and Border Lakes Natural Area around 840 PM CDT.
Boulder Junction around 850 PM CDT.
Johnson Lake Barrens Natural Area around 855 PM CDT.

Other locations impacted by this strong thunderstorm include
Manitowish Waters, Presque Isle, Big Lake Campground, Van Vliet
Hemlocks Natural Area, Jag Lake Campground, Upper Gresham Lake
Campground, Dunn Lake Natural Area, High Lake Natural Area, North
Trout Lake Campground and Trout Lake.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 28 at 8:05PM CDT until October 28 at 8:45PM CDT by NWS Midland/Odessa TX
properties.description:
At 804 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 23 miles southeast
of Pine Springs, moving north at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect wind
damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

This severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly rural areas of north
central Culberson County.
properties.instruction:
Prepare immediately for large hail and damaging winds. People outside
should move to a shelter, inside a strong building and away from
windows.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Move indoors immediately. Lightning is one of nature's leading
killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder, you are close enough to
be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 11:51AM MDT until October 30 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Grande at Embudo affecting Rio Arriba and Taos Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Embudo.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Minor overbank flows are occurring above the
Embudo gaging site. Access to riverside picnic facilities above
Pilar and below the Taos Junction Bridge along State Route 570 will
be limited if further rises occur. Water may be extremely close to
underside of bridge over Rio Grande on Aguas Caliente Rd in Pilar.
Other localized effects due to the high water levels will begin to
be felt at a stage of 10 feet but no significant flooding is
expected until the river rises to 12 feet.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday the stage was 7.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.1 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Action stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 11:45AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Wednesday was 6.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain between 6.4 and 6.7
feet through the next several days.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.7
feet on 07/21/2009.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 9:03AM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Upstream persistent gusty northeast winds and tidal effects on the
St John River are slowing flow. At Deland, the river is forecast to
crest near Minor Flood Stage the next couple days, then begin a slow
decline through Action Stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
the next couple days. It will then fall below flood stage late in
the week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 28 at 8:58AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds and upstream tidal effects are
slowing river flow on the St Johns River at Astor. River levels are
forecast to begin a slow decline late this week, but remain in
Moderate Flood stage for at least the next couple weeks.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Moderate flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to crest around 3.8 feet
this week, then begin a gradual decline late in the week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 200 AM EDT.
